content: Snapshot/approval testing architecture: separates 'produce a canonical serialized artifact' from 'compare against a stored approved artifact', with the comparison typically being naive text/structural diff, not policy-aware. Known failure mode discussed in industry sources (e.g. TigerBeetle's 'snapshot testing for the masses', Jest docs): snapshots drift across environments/platforms unless a single canonical producer (e.g. CI runner) is authoritative, and reviewers rubber-stamp diffs without scrutiny ('snapshot blindness'). mediadiff's fingerprint+policy-comparison model differs from naive snapshot testing in exactly the way needed to avoid this failure mode: comparison is not raw text diff but semantic (per check_id, per semantic type, under tolerance), which prevents blind approval of accidental byte differences -- but the general snapshot ecosystem confirms canonical-artifact-first design is standard and cross-platform non-determinism in the producer is the #1 real-world failure mode to guard against (relevant to mediadiff's idempotence guarantee).
